To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ventricular repolarisation memory can lead to the development of pseudo-primary T waves and that these can be reversed by a second exposure to the same stimulus, resulting in the normalization of ventricular repololarization.

ventricular depolarisation memory (T wave memory) can be manifested in the form of pseudo-primary T wave, pseudo-primary T waves that reverse to become primary, and pseudo-primary T wave with a reversal of primary T waves, and that ventricular repolarisation memory can be induced by different conditions, such as ventricular pacing, intraventricular conduction disturbances, ventricular pre-excitation, tachyarrhytthmias, and even by the presence of a pacemaker

“T wave memory” is the phenomenon of ventricular repolari-zation remodeling caused by the previous exposure of the ventricular myocardial cells to the same stimuli and that it can induce pseudo-primary T waves and/or reversal of primary and secondary T waves.

T wave memory is a peculiar variety and consequence of cardiac remodeling caused, in the vast majority of cases, by a transient change of the course of ventriculardepolarization.
ventricular repolarisation memory is a peculiar variety, or a consequence, of cardiac remodeling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T wave “memory effect” is an important factor that must be taken into consideration when analyzing the electrocardiograms.
ventricular repolarizaton memory is a phenomenon that should be taken into account in order to interpret accurately the ECG.

the electrocardiogram (ECG) should be interpreted in a dynamic fashion.
